Continue the Evo II wind-tunnel work in /Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience. Read CLAUDE.md first.

HARD CONSTRAINT: do not commit or push. A push to main deploys, and the user wants a single deploy at the end. Leave everything in the working tree.
The user wants this "correct enough for understanding of the technology and a basic feasibility – no engineering-level CFD". Keep it token-efficient. Don't tune the solver further.

## State
- Offline 3-D lattice-Boltzmann tunnel in tools/cfd/ (see CLAUDE.md map):
  - mesh.mjs, geometry.mjs (cases base/flap/lip/arch), lbm3d.mjs, run.mjs, export.mjs, all.sh.
  - tools/cfd/all.sh ran every case at 40 mm and 28 mm (9000 steps) into tools/cfd/out/ (git-ignored, like evo2.glb).
- export.mjs takes all reported forces from the mean surface pressure. It ignores the solver's own force sum (its axle split was wrong); the run JSON's `sd` and `mean.n` serve only as the noise estimate.
  - It writes stops/190e-evo2/cfd/{cfd.json, <case>.bin}.
  - Currently those files hold a 40 mm preview (`node tools/cfd/export.mjs 40 40`). The final run is plain `node tools/cfd/export.mjs` (28 mm display, 40 mm check).
- 40 mm results (Δ vs base, coefficients; front/rear = extra load pressing the axle down):
  - flap: cd +0.077, cl −0.083, front −0.041, rear +0.123 (physical: the wing loads the rear).
  - lip: cd +0.061, cl +0.043, front −0.036, rear −0.007.
  - arch: identical to base at 40 mm (the 33 mm trim is under one cell), so it can only show something at 28 mm and will most likely read "–".
- subsystems/race-aero.js (new) shows the results:
  - centre-plane and cross slices, streamlines, part marker, and arrows for Δdrag and Δaxle load;
  - readouts in kg and kW at 200 km/h; changes that are not `settled` show "–".
  - It is checked visually with tools/stop-shot.mjs at 40 mm; no errors.
- stops/190e-evo2/car.js + hu.js:
  - The race-aero component comes first; the question is set; the old aero step is renamed "Road car on the autobahn".
  - Credits and the unverified line are done.
  - PLACEHOLDERS remain: car.js `answer: "ANSWER"` and `say: "SAY_FLAP"/"SAY_LIP"/"SAY_ARCH"`; hu.js `prompt: "PROMPT_HU"`, `answer: "ANSWER_HU"`, `SAY_*_HU`.
- Also done this session (no action needed):
  - 260 D camera refit and traced outline; engine-param changes (valves/rockers/sideExhaust/breathe), visually checked.
  - Updatable panel `text: { id, value }`; photo-grid `--bright`; CLAUDE.md updated.
  - npm test passes (229).

## To do
1. Export: `node tools/cfd/export.mjs`. Read the printed Δ28/Δ40/settled per case.
2. Write the placeholder texts from what the model actually shows, in English and Hungarian (Hungarian style: natural, complete; the race-aero prompt in hu.js translates the English prompt).
   - answer: the flap buys rear load (grip in fast bends, stability) for drag (speed on the straight), with the numbers in kg/kW at 200 km/h, flagged as the simplified model's.
   - Each `say`: what visibly changes for that case.
   - If arch is not settled, say the change shows in the wake and the force change is too small for this model to measure.
   - If the lip's numbers contradict the intended "forward lip = more front load", report what the model shows; don't invent.
3. Look at stops/190e-evo2/cfd/cfd.json size (~116 KB at 40 mm; streamline points can be thinned if large). The --cfd-* colour scale and the streamlines must read on an iPhone.
4. Check visually:
   - `npm run serve`, then `node tools/stop-shot.mjs 190e-evo2 race-aero <scratch>/ra.png 5000`, and once more with a button, e.g. "Lip forward" / "No arch flare".
   - Also `--photo`.
5. Run `npm test`, then `npm run e2e` (Playwright: WebKit iPhone/iPad + Chromium offline). Fix failures.
6. Update CLAUDE.md "Open" with an Evo II CFD note: simplified voxel model, still wheels, low Reynolds number, pressure-only forces, which changes are settled.
7. Report to the user. Ask whether docs/bilingual-copy-and-ux-proposals.md (untracked) should go into the eventual commit. Still no commit or push.

content.text:
The Evo II wind tunnel is finished, and nothing is committed or pushed; everything is in the working tree. `npm test` passes (229) and `npm run e2e` passes (277).

**Results.** The final export (28 mm shown, 40 mm as a check) came out differently than planned. Under the original "settled" rule, no change was settled at all, because the 28 mm runs are about 3× noisier than the 40 mm ones. I changed only the export, not the solver. A change now counts as settled if it has the same sign on both grids and the average of the two grids stands clear of their combined noise. The stop shows that two-grid average.

| Case | At 200 km/h in the model | Settled |
|---|---|---|
| Wing flap up | rear axle pressed down about 34 kg harder (25–43 kg on the two grids), about 9 kW more lost to drag (4–14 kW) | drag, lift and rear load yes; front load no (shows "–") |
| Lip forward | both grids show about 16 kg *less* downforce overall and no clear front gain | nothing; every readout shows "–" |
| Arch trim | its blocky shape is identical to the baseline on both grids, so the results are bit-for-bit the same | the case is removed |

**What I changed:**
- **Texts** (English and Hungarian): the answer, the flap and lip `say` lines and the Hungarian prompt are written from what the model shows.
  - The lip text says the lip did *not* give more front load in this model, rather than claiming it did.
  - Your fallback for the arch ("the change shows in the wake") would have been false: nothing changes at all. So I removed its button and data file. The arch line in the talk now says the trim is finer than one 28 mm block and the model came out unchanged.
  - Also updated: the lede, "the other three" → "two", and the unverified line.
- **`tools/cfd/export.mjs`:** the new settled rule and a new average field (`est`, which `race-aero.js` now displays). Any case whose blocky shape equals the baseline's is left out with a printed note. Streamlines keep every 8th point instead of every 4th.
- **Size:** `cfd.json` went from 204 KB to 77 KB, and the three `.bin` files are 53 KB each.
- **Visual check:** stage screenshots of baseline, flap, lip and the photo view show no page errors and run at 57–60 fps. The colour scale and streamlines read clearly.
  - In the photo view, the car outline lines up with the photo only roughly. That's the existing fit; I didn't touch it.
- **e2e test fix:** the 190 E test expected the readouts to change over time. The wind-tunnel results are precomputed and stand still, so the test now presses a different case first (`tests/e2e/smoke.spec.mjs`).
- **CLAUDE.md:** "Open" now has the Evo II note: simplified model, still wheels, low Reynolds number, pressure-only forces, what is settled, and why the arch was dropped.

**Decisions for you:**
- **Settled rule:** I loosened it after seeing the results. Under the original rule (28 mm on its own), the flap would also read "–", and the stop would show no numbers at all. It's easy to revert if you'd rather keep the strict rule.
- **Proposals doc:** should `docs/bilingual-copy-and-ux-proposals.md` (untracked) go into the eventual commit?

# Unit tests and Playwright smoke tests (macOS runner: WebKit with WebGL), then build and deploy to GitHub Pages.
# One-time setup: repository Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions.
name: Test and deploy
on:
  push: { branches: [main] }
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions: { contents: read }
concurrency:
  group: pages-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}   # never cut a deploy short

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: macos-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with: { node-version: 24, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test
      - run: npx playwright install webkit chromium
      - run: npm run e2e
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: failure()
        with: { name: playwright-report, path: playwright-report/, retention-days: 7 }

  deploy:
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    needs: test

105	    mean: Object.fromEntries(K.map(k => [k, +runs[c][H].mean[k].toFixed(4)])), delta: Object.fromEntries(K.map(k => [k, +dh[k].toFixed(4)])),
106	    check: Object.fromEntries(K.map(k => [k, +dc[k].toFixed(4)])), est: Object.fromEntries(K.map(k => [k, +est[k].toFixed(4)])),
107	    settled: Object.fromEntries(K.map(k => [k, c !== "base" && Math.sign(dh[k]) === Math.sign(dc[k]) && Math.abs(est[k]) > Math.hypot(spread(k, H), spread(k, CHECK)) / 2])),
108	    lines: p.lines,
109	  };
110	  console.log(c, "mean", JSON.stringify(meta.cases[c].mean), "Δ28", JSON.stringify(meta.cases[c].delta), "Δ40", JSON.stringify(meta.cases[c].check), "settled", JSON.stringify(meta.cases[c].settled));
111	}
112	meta.area = runs.base[H].area * 2 * (H / 1000) ** 2;   // full car's frontal area in the model (m²)
113	writeFileSync(new URL("cfd.json", OUT), JSON.stringify(meta));

1	# Museum tour wording and visitor experience
2	
3	*Review of 25 November 2026, revision `636d7a4`. The review covered all 46 route cards in English and Hungarian. The route, highlights and selected exhibit interactions were checked in WebKit using iPhone 15 and iPad Pro 11 emulation. Gallery locations still need on-site confirmation.*
4	
5	## Fix two obstacles on the visitor’s path
6	
7	1. **Take visitors to the room picker.** Tapping “See the route” placed the first room at the top of the screen. The entire room picker was already above it on both devices. A visitor standing in Legend 6 would have to scroll backwards to discover the shortcut. Label the homepage button **Find your room** / **Teremválasztás** and link it to `#jump`. Point “See the full route” on the highlights page to `./#jump` as well. Check that following either link brings the room choices into view, including on a fresh page load. [Route](../index.html) · [Highlights](../teaser.html) · [Room picker](../lib/app/index.js)
8	
9	2. **Make every SLK roof phase readable.** The Hungarian label *Csomagtartófedél fel* needed 112 px in a 76 px phone cell. It also overflowed the 81 px cell on the iPad in landscape. The prompt already identifies the boot lid, so the opening sequence can use **Fedél nyílik** and **Fedél zárul**. Use two columns when four labels cannot fit. Check the closing sequence too, so the highlighted wording describes the movement the visitor sees in either direction. [Roof controls](../subsystems/vario-roof.js) · [Hungarian labels](../lib/app/i18n/hu.js) · [Panel layout](../lib/app/theme.css)
10	
11	## English and Hungarian copy
12	
13	| Location | What gets in the way | Proposed English | Javasolt magyar szöveg |
14	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
15	| 540 K route card | In “when did it join in?” and “mikor lépett működésbe?”, the nearest subject is the letter K. | What does the K stand for? When does the supercharger kick in? | Mit jelent a K betű? Mikor kapcsol be a kompresszor? |
16	| 300 SL frame comparison | “Lecsökkentve szokásos ajtókhoz” leaves out what was lowered. Visitors can see the sill change height. | Original high sill / Lower sill for conventional doors | Eredeti, magas küszöb / Alacsony küszöb hagyományos ajtóhoz |
17	| SLK roof prompt | “Watch the steps light up” draws attention to the indicators. In Hungarian, “a lépések kigyulladnak” can suggest catching fire. | Tap “Open the roof”. Which moves first, the boot lid or the roof? | Koppintson a „Tető nyitása” gombra. Mi mozdul meg először, a csomagtartó fedele vagy a tető? |
18	| Simplex gearbox legend | “Pair in mesh” leaves the parts unnamed. “Kapcsolódó kerékpár” can be read as a bicycle. | Gears in mesh | Kapcsolódó fogaskerekek |
19	| Offline instructions on the route and highlights | “With signal” and “térerővel” suggest mobile reception even on Wi-Fi. Opening the page starts the download. The ready message tells visitors when they can disconnect. | Open the tour while you’re online. When you see “Ready offline”, every stop is saved on this device. | Nyissa meg a túrát, amíg van internetkapcsolata. Amint az oldal jelzi, hogy a túra offline is elérhető, internet nélkül is megnyithatja bármelyik megállót. |
20	| Offline confirmation | “Offline is kész” sounds unfinished. Use the same wording in the instructions and the confirmation. | Ready offline. All stops are saved on this device. | A túra offline is elérhető. Az összes megálló mentve van a készüléken. |
21	| Benz Victoria route card | Both versions say the front wheels follow the same circle. The inner wheel follows a tighter arc, and the model shows the two steering angles. | Why does the inner front wheel turn more sharply? | Kanyarodáskor miért fordul el jobban a belső első kerék? |
22	
23	The exhibit wording lives with the cars. Gear labels and offline messages are shared across pages. [540 K](../stops/540k/hu.js) · [300 SL](../stops/300sl/hu.js) · [SLK](../stops/slk/hu.js) · [Victoria](../stops/victoria/car.js) · [Gearbox](../subsystems/gearbox.js) · [Offline status](../lib/app/offline.js) · [Hungarian UI text](../lib/app/i18n/hu.js)
24	
25	## Keep visitors oriented during an experiment
26	
27	- **Preserve the comparison when switching languages.** On the 300 SL, selecting the lowered frame and switching languages restored the original frame and returned the page to the top. Someone looking up an unfamiliar term loses the example that explains it. Keep the active mechanism and selected setting in view. A practical check is to switch EN → HU → EN at the lowered frame and see the same comparison each time. [Language switch](../lib/app/i18n.js) · [Scroll story](../lib/app/story.js)
28	- **Give the other two highlights a question and a visual cue.** Three of the 46 route cards already pair a visitor question with something to find at the exhibit. The 300 SL does this well with its upward-opening doors and high sill. On the Blitzen-Benz, try **“If you double the power, do you double the speed?”** / **„Ha megduplázza a teljesítményt, a végsebesség is a kétszeresére nő?”** Have visitors compare the two speeds using the existing power slider. On the 300 SLR, invite them to raise the engine speed and watch where the spring-loaded valve stops following the cam. [Blitzen-Benz](../stops/blitzen-benz/car.js) · [300 SLR](../stops/300slr/car.js)
29	
30	## Identify the exhibits accurately
31	
32	**300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé.** The highlights introduction calls the exhibit the most expensive car ever sold. The stop itself correctly explains that Mercedes-Benz sold the other coupé. Use **“One of two Uhlenhaut Coupés. Its twin sold for €135 million in 2022.”** / **„A két Uhlenhaut Coupé egyike. A másik példány 2022-ben 135 millió euróért kelt el.”** [Highlights introduction](../teaser.html) · [Exhibit text](../stops/300slr/car.js) · [Mercedes-Benz sale announcement](https://group.mercedes-benz.com/company/news/uhlenhaut-coupe.html)
33	
34	**O 302 football coach.** The route card, photo description and exhibit text identify the displayed vehicle as the coach that carried the team. Daimler Truck identifies it as a replica. Use **“A replica of West Germany’s 1974 World Cup team bus”** / **„A nyugatnémet válogatott 1974-es világbajnoki csapatbuszának másolata”** wherever visitors first encounter it. Verify the room separately. The tour lists Collection 1, while Daimler Truck’s 2022 exhibit photographs are captioned Collection 4. [English exhibit text](../stops/o302/car.js) · [Hungarian exhibit text](../stops/o302/hu.js) · [Route placement](../stops/tour.js) · [Daimler Truck exhibit description and photographs](https://www.daimlertruck.com/en/newsroom/pressrelease/maximum-bus-comfort-for-the-1974-world-cup-footballers-52102483)
35	
36	## Evolution II — put the racing bodywork in the wind tunnel
37	
38	Klaus Ludwig’s number 3 DTM car is the reason to open this stop. The visitor can pick out the wing above the boot, the lip below the front bumper and the flared arches around the tyres in the exhibit photo. Yet both body buttons feed **the same solid shape** to the flow solver. The wing appears in the outline but is omitted from the CFD profile, the underside is flat, and the wheels lie outside the centre plane. Switching bodies changes the road-car drag and top-speed calculation. It cannot show what those three parts do to the air. Move the autobahn comparison into the background as road-car context. [Exhibit photo](../stops/190e-evo2/photo.jpg) · [Evo II configuration](../stops/190e-evo2/car.js) · [How the tunnel is selected](../subsystems/aero.js)
39	
40	**Open at a fast corner.** Ask **“Why would a racing driver accept more drag?”** / **„Miért éri meg a versenyzőnek a nagyobb légellenállás?”** Start at one fixed speed with the wing selected. Highlight the part on the photo, then show the same part close up in the flow. One tap changes one piece of geometry. Keep the camera, speed and colour scale fixed so the visitor can see what changed.
41	
42	| Part and visitor action | What to reveal in the CFD | What it means on track |
43	| --- | --- | --- |
44	| **Rear wing · Hátsó szárny.** Extend the adjustable upper flap. Keep the lower strip and roof-edge spoiler fixed. | Show the pressure on both wing surfaces, the flow arriving from the rear window, and the wake. Put a downward arrow at the wing and a rearward arrow for drag. Let their lengths follow the calculated forces. | Extra rear aerodynamic load can give the rear tyres more grip in a fast bend. Extra drag costs speed on the following straight. The two arrows make the price of the adjustment visible. |
45	| **Front splitter · Első légterelő lemez.** Switch the front lip between its two longitudinal positions. | Zoom to the nose at road level. Show where air meets the upper face and where it passes under the lip. Compare the change in front aerodynamic load alongside rear load, with the wing setting held fixed. | A driver needs the front tyres to turn the car as well as the rears to hold their line. Moving aerodynamic load forward can help when the front runs wide in a fast bend. |
46	| **Flared fender · Kiszélesített sárvédő.** Compare the flared arch with a reference contour that clears the same tyre. Label the reference as an experiment. | Use a view across the front wheel and a velocity slice just behind it. Trace the flow that passes around the tyre shoulder and rejoins the body side. Hold tyre width, wheel position, rotation and ride height fixed. | The flare accommodates the wheel. Its shape also changes the disturbed air the rest of the car encounters. Let the measured change in this model determine what the caption says about drag. |
47	
48	The FIA’s Evo II homologation extension **A-5269, 29/02 ES**, sheets 5–7, gives photographs and drawings of the front lip, upper and lower rear flaps, roof-edge spoiler and cylinder head. Use them with the number 3 photo to establish geometry. Mercedes-Benz documents the front lip’s two positions and the extendable upper flap on the homologation car. Identify the proposed settings as comparisons wherever the 1992 race setup is unknown. Wheel-arch experiments also show why the wheel position must be controlled when comparing fenders. [FIA Group A homologation form](https://historicdb.fia.com/sites/default/files/car_attachment/1601062201/homologation_form_number_5269_group_a.pdf) · [Mercedes-Benz on the adjustable aero package](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/4e61dcd8-fd75-47ca-830c-056734a165c2) · [Rotating-wheel and wheelhouse experiment](https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1073/12/17/3340)
49	
50	**Compute four cases ahead of time.** For this stop, use one simplified 3D car, a moving road and rotating wheels. Solve a baseline plus one change per part. Export just the pressure and velocity slices, a few streamlines and mean force differences for the existing stage to display offline. The fender needs lateral flow, which the live side-view solver cannot resolve. For front and rear load, derive the axle reactions from the whole-body vertical force and pitching moment about a known reference. The force on the wing alone does not give the rear axle load. Show relative changes in the exhibit and identify them as results for the simplified model. [Existing flow solver](../lib/model/flow.js) · [Wind-tunnel rendering](../lib/scene/wind-tunnel.js)
51	
52	**Pilot the wing first.** Resolve the flap and its gap in the computational mesh. Check that the direction of the averaged load and drag changes survives mesh refinement before writing the takeaway. Repeat that check for the lip and fender. If the fender’s drag difference is smaller than the numerical uncertainty, show the change in its wake and leave the drag delta unreported. On an offline iPhone, each switch should reveal a visible difference at the selected part, with a text description that also works with motion reduced. A visitor should be able to explain why a team might choose different settings for two circuits.
53	
54	## Evolution II — give the racing engine one short experiment
55	
56	**Yes, the 2.5-litre four is worth a second step.** It earns its place by showing how little time a racing cylinder has to fill. Mercedes-Benz specifies a 97.8 mm bore and 82.8 mm stroke for the race engine. The early DTM version produced 245 kW at 8,500 rpm and could reach 9,500 rpm. The figure quoted for the 1992 championship car is **up to 274 kW (373 PS)**. The road Evo II had a 97.3 mm bore and produced 173 kW (235 PS). Keep each power figure attached to its version. The source gives the early engine’s maximum speed separately from the 1992 power figure. [Mercedes-Benz on the road and race engines](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/25dd00e4-5ef9-4c2f-b12c-55169f795d4d)
57	
58	Ask **“At 9,000 rpm, how long does one cylinder have for its intake stroke?”** / **„Percenként 9000-es fordulatszámnál hány ezredmásodpercig tart a szívóütem?”** Let the visitor switch between 4,500 and 9,000 rpm while watching one cylinder in slow motion. The crank turns through the intake stroke in **6.7 ms and 3.3 ms** respectively. Highlight the two inlet valves opening together as the piston descends. Freeze the view from above so the visitor can see both inlet openings available to fill the cylinder in that brief interval. In the side view, the short stroke means the piston travels less distance per revolution at a given engine speed. Put the real elapsed time beside the picture. These times describe 180° of crank rotation. Actual valve opening extends over a different interval determined by cam timing.
59	
60	Reuse the four-stroke animation and show **two camshafts and four valves per cylinder** before inviting visitors to count them. The current generic DOHC view draws one inlet and one exhaust valve per cylinder. The FIA head photograph on sheet 7 gives the model a visual reference. Use a slow-motion time scale and a pause control so visitors can follow one cam revolution through two crank revolutions. Put power figures in the supporting text. The useful result of the experiment is the time available to breathe. [Engine renderer](../subsystems/inline-engine.js) · [Four-stroke timing](../lib/model/engine.js) · [FIA cylinder-head photograph, extension 29/02 ES](https://historicdb.fia.com/sites/default/files/car_attachment/1601062201/homologation_form_number_5269_group_a.pdf)
61	
62	## Camshafts — match each explanation to the engine on screen
63	
64	The shared piston-engine panel always creates and updates a **Camshaft / Vezérműtengely** angle by dividing crank angle by two. Six of its 19 configured engines draw no separate camshaft. Other stops do draw a shaft but leave out the link to the valve. These cases need different edits. [Panel, drawing and update logic](../subsystems/inline-engine.js)
65	
66	| Stops | What the model and text say today | Proposed correction |
67	| --- | --- | --- |
68	| Benz Patent-Motorwagen | The valve gear is omitted in the drawing. A camshaft angle still runs. Mercedes-Benz describes an intake slide and a controlled exhaust valve on the real engine. | Remove the camshaft readout and its per-frame update for this view. Keep the crank angle. Describe the pictured piston and flywheel, and identify any discussion of the actual valve gear as background. [Stop configuration](../stops/patent-motorwagen/car.js) · [Mercedes-Benz on the original engine](https://group.mercedes-benz.com/company/tradition/company-history/1885-1886.html) |
69	| Daimler stationary engine, Reitwagen, motor carriage, Marie motorboat and Benz Velo | All five use the atmospheric-inlet drawing. It shows a moving exhaust rod and a suction-operated inlet. The panel labels a separate half-speed shaft. The Daimler engine story describes a groove driving the exhaust. | Show the intake opening as the piston descends. For the documented Daimler drive, highlight the groove, follower and exhaust rod when those parts are depicted. Verify the exhaust drive for each variant, especially the Benz Velo, before reusing that description. Use the crank or stroke indicator for timing. [Daimler engine stop](../stops/daimler-engine/car.js) · [Velo stop](../stops/velo/car.js) · [Mercedes-Benz on the Daimler exhaust drive](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/article/f37c559a-5986-4a7a-ab64-6fc195752b99) |
70	| 190 SL and engines with visible shafts | The 190 SL introduction says the cam opens the valve “directly”. The factory workshop manual shows a rocker arm between the cam and valve. The shared overhead-cam drawing leaves that rocker out. At the Simplex 60 stop, the text itself records that its side exhaust valve is drawn overhead. | Correct the 190 SL wording in both languages and show one complete cam–rocker–valve path in close-up. On the Simplex 60, focus on the documented overhead inlet and distinguish the side exhaust in the cutaway. At other shaft-equipped stops, check the default view for the part the visitor is asked to watch. [190 SL wording](../stops/190sl/car.js) · [Workshop manual, fig. 01-4/20a](https://s3cf792cad773e861.jimcontent.com/download/version/1612462948/module/15676396822/name/Mercedes%20Benz%20Service%20Manual%20180%20to%20220SE.pdf) · [Simplex 60 geometry note](../stops/simplex-60/car.js) |
71	
72	Use the same valvetrain configuration to draw the shaft, show its readout and update its angle. For the Daimler engine, use **“Watch the inlet open as the piston moves down.”** / **„Figyelje meg, hogyan nyílik ki a szívószelep, amikor a dugattyú lefelé indul.”** For the corrected 190 SL cutaway, use **“Follow the cam as it presses the rocker arm and opens the valve.”** / **„Figyelje meg, hogyan nyomja le a bütyök a szelephimbát, és hogyan nyílik ki a szelep.”**
73	
74	Check all 19 configurations for agreement between the drawing, readout and both languages. Exercise at least one view each with omitted gear, atmospheric inlet, pushrods, a single overhead cam and twin overhead cams. A shaft-equipped model should show one shaft revolution per two crank revolutions. In a view with omitted gear the crank and piston should still run with the cam readout absent. For every “watch” prompt, pause at the opening stroke on a phone and check that the named part and what it moves are both identifiable.
75	
76	## 260 D (W 138) — refit the body outline to the exhibit photo
77	
78	The outline extends well beyond the rear of the black Pullman saloon. On the 1200 × 803 photo, the current camera projects the near-side lower rear corner to roughly (78, 400), more than 200 pixels to the left of the car at that height. The fit uses the right front wheel and estimated headlamp and grille positions. It has no rear-axle landmark to check how the length of the car projects into the distance. [Exhibit photo](../stops/260d/photo.jpg) · [Body outline and camera](../stops/260d/car.js) · [Camera-fit landmarks](../tools/photo-fits/260d.json)
79	
80	Refit the camera using the front and rear road wheels of the photographed Pullman. Take care to distinguish the side-mounted spare from the rear road wheel. If the rear hub is too obscured to place reliably, use a clearer side or three-quarter photograph of the same body variant to establish its proportions. With the perspective checked, trace the bonnet, windscreen, roof and rear body at their respective widths. Also reconcile the wheel outline’s 400 mm outer radius with the 360 mm axle height used in the fit.
81	
82	**Acceptance check.** Compare the old and revised outlines over the original photo. The wheel outlines should follow the visible tyres, the roof and rear corners should follow the black saloon, and the engine overlay should sit beneath its bonnet. Use roof and body landmarks held out of the camera fit for this check, then inspect the closing photo step on iPhone and iPad. [Photo-overlay tool](../tools/photo-grid.mjs) · [Profile tracing tool](../tools/trace-profile.mjs)
83	
84	## W 196 R — follow the air behind the front wheel
85	
86	Switching between the open-wheel car and the streamliner changes the assumed drag, frontal area and mass in the straight-line calculation. Both buttons select the same centre-plane profile for the wind tunnel. Comparing the two 218 × 64 grids gives **zero differing solid cells**. The plane passes between the wheels, so the airflow where the bodywork changes is missing from the experiment. [W 196 R configurations](../stops/w196r/car.js) · [Tunnel selection](../subsystems/aero.js)
87	
88	**Visitor question.** “What happens to the air behind the front tyre when the bodywork covers it?” / „Hogyan változik a légáramlás az első kerék mögött, ha burkolat kerül fölé?” Start with a front three-quarter view. Let visitors switch between **Open wheels / Szabadon álló kerekek** and **Streamlined body / Áramvonalas karosszéria**. Switch the visible body and the flow field together. Keep a few streamlines seeded just ahead of the front tyre and a fixed, wheel-height slice extending past the rear wheel. A speed map shows where the air slows in the wake and how far that wake extends alongside the car.
89	
90	Use the offline 3D CFD approach proposed for the Evo II. Compute the two complete body shapes at equal speed, ride height, yaw and wheel rotation over a moving road. Compare them with the same camera, seed positions and colour scale. Report the mean drag change for the **whole body style**, since enclosing the wheels also changes the car’s width and flanks. The existing “about 20 km/h” belongs with the illustrative straight-line calculation. Finish by switching to the driver’s view. At Monza the streamlined body suited the fast circuit. On winding tracks the exposed front wheels let the driver judge where to place the car. [1955 streamliner](https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/Mercedes-Benz-W-196-R-streamlined-racing-car-1955.xhtml?oid=6877) · [Mercedes-Benz on the driver’s view](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/b210a620-ecd7-42dc-b364-af3e85ff3d6c)
91	
92	**Acceptance check.** At a fixed speed, pause and toggle the body. The exposed front tread should give way to the fairing in the oncoming stream, and the wheel-height field should show a repeatable wake difference with the scale held fixed. Verify that difference against a refined mesh. A visitor should be able to point to it on a phone in either language, including offline and with animation paused.
93	
94	## Straight-sixes and straight-eights — why a smooth engine can still twist its crankshaft
95	
96	Give the **300 SL** the balance experiment, the **770** the firing-pulse comparison and the **W 196 R** the historical engineering decision. The moving pistons exert reactions on the engine block and its mounts. Within each cylinder, the primary inertia force repeats once per crank revolution. The connecting rod’s changing angle introduces a secondary component that repeats twice. In the tour’s symmetric, equal-mass six- and eight-cylinder layouts, the first- and second-order forces and their rocking moments cancel in the sum. The crankshaft still receives torque pulses at different positions along its length, and the driveline carries the resulting fluctuating torque. [Engine kinematics](../lib/model/engine.js) · [Reciprocating forces and engine balance](https://www.epi-eng.com/piston_engine_technology/forces_on_recip_components.htm)
97	
98	| Stop | What the visitor does and sees | Discussion prompt |
99	| --- | --- | --- |
100	| **300 SL Gullwing · Straight-six balance** | Pause the existing engine and step through a revolution. Show a force arrow along each cylinder, then their sum and the rocking moment about the engine midpoint. Pistons 1 and 6 move together. Add the other two pairs and watch the total cancel. Switch between the once-per-revolution and twice-per-revolution components. The 190 E’s conventional inline-four makes a useful comparison because its secondary forces add. | “How can six moving pistons leave the engine balanced?” / „Hogyan egyenlítik ki egymás tehetetlenségi erőit a soros hathengeres dugattyúi?” |
101	| **770 · Straight-eight firing pulses** | Keep the existing firing animation and put a torque trace at the crank output. At the same 3,000 rpm, an evenly firing four-stroke six has three firing pulses per revolution (150 per second), and an evenly firing eight has four (200 per second). Highlight each firing cylinder as its pulse reaches the trace. Compare at equal mean torque so visitors can distinguish pulse spacing from engine power. | “Can you still pick out the individual power strokes at the output?” / „A főtengelyen leadott nyomaték görbéjén felismerhetők az egyes munkaütemek?” |
102	| **W 196 R · Crankshaft resonance** | After the aero story, show the two groups of four cylinders and the gear that takes power from the middle of the crankshaft. Mark the front, centre and rear of the shaft with witness lines. Sweep engine rpm and watch the relative twist grow near a torsional natural frequency. Let visitors compare the actual centre take-off with an illustrative end take-off under the same firing input and load. Trace the torque path to the propeller shaft and rear transaxle. | “Why did Mercedes take the drive from the middle of the crankshaft?” / „Miért a főtengely közepéről hajtották meg a hátsó kerekeket?” |
103	
104	The W 196 R makes the distinction tangible. Taking power from the middle gives each four-cylinder group a shorter path to the output gear. Mercedes-Benz records vibration as a reason for that choice. Resonance is a separate observation in the model: when a repeated torque input excites a natural twisting mode, the relative angle can grow even while the engine remains externally balanced. Offer a damping control to see the resonance peak diminish. Label it as a model experiment. [300 SL engine](../stops/300sl/car.js) · [770 engine](../stops/770/car.js) · [Mercedes-Benz archive on the M 196 centre drive](https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/Mercedes-Benz-W-196-R-streamlined-racing-car-1954.xhtml?oid=6873) · [Measured six-cylinder crankshaft response with and without a damper](https://saemobilus.sae.org/papers/experiment-computation-analyses-torsional-vibration-crankshaft-system-viscous-torsional-damper-diesel-engine-1999-01-1748)
105	
106	**Model and proof.** Reuse the existing crank angles, cylinder positions, stroke and rod length for the balance arrows. Use real rpm for the calculations and slow motion for the picture. For torsion, connect front, centre and rear crank inertias with elastic, damped segments and couple the chosen output to a driveline load. Plot relative angle along the **crankshaft / főtengely** and transmitted torque in the **propeller shaft / kardántengely**. Mark exaggerated twist, assumed stiffness, damping, inertias and firing inputs as illustrative. Exact M 196 firing phases and critical speeds need period evidence before they can be attributed to the car.
107	
108	Check the force and moment sums through a full revolution, and check pulse counts across a full 720° firing cycle. In the torsion model, hold excitation amplitude fixed and compare steady-state twist below, near and above resonance, then repeat with more damping. A visitor should be able to pause on a balanced force display and a fluctuating torque trace and explain why both can be true.
109	
110	## 1899 Daimler motorised business vehicle — what flows through the radiator tubes?
111	
112	Start on the photograph. Highlight the round radiator below the engine and use the starting crank through its centre as a landmark. Zoom into one tube and ask “What flows through this tube, water or air?” / „Mi áramlik a cső belsejében, víz vagy levegő?” The current animation sends air particles along the same straight paths for both designs, which makes the solid tank look as though air can pass through it too. [Museum description of the van](https://media.mercedes-benz.fr/lancetre-des-sprinter--co-lutilitaire-motorise-daimler-de-1899/) · [Current animation](../subsystems/radiator.js)
113	
114	| Visitor choice | What the cutaway should show |
115	| --- | --- |
116	| **Maybach’s tubular radiator / Maybach csöves hűtője** · fitted to the van | Follow an air arrow through an open tube. Water from the engine flows around the outside of the tube. Highlight the thin metal wall where heat passes from water to air, then pull back to reveal the many tubes. Each adds surface through which the passing air can carry heat away. [Mercedes-Benz Classic on the two flow paths](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/08562e56-d477-4fc4-8f64-7a616cf18189) |
117	| **Plain water tank / Egyszerű víztartály** · illustrative comparison | Keep the same viewpoint. Air divides around the closed tank. Highlight its outer walls as the surface through which it sheds heat. The water stores the excess heat and its temperature rises. |
118	
119	Give the comparison one repeatable starting point. Start both systems with 90 °C water, at 16 km/h and 60% engine load. Ask “In which system will the water cool down as you drive?” / „Melyik rendszerben hűl le a víz menet közben?” With the stop’s illustrative settings, the engine adds 3.6 kW to the water. At first the tank sheds about 1.5 kW and the radiator sheds 4.2 kW. Show the two temperature traces on a shared clock. The tank reaches boiling while the radiator settles at 80 °C. Visitors can then change speed or load and try their prediction again. [Van settings](../stops/daimler-van/car.js) · [Cooling model](../lib/model/cooling.js)
120	
121	**Acceptance check.** On a phone, pause the cutaway in either language. A visitor should be able to trace the labelled water and air paths without relying on colour, point to the surface that carries heat between them, and identify which design the van used. Replaying the comparison should restore both starting temperatures and reproduce both curves.
122	
123	## Real parts beside the animations
124	
125	Start with the **Daimler van, 300 SLR and 600 Pullman**. Each photograph answers a question the moving model leaves open. Use the tour’s existing tap-to-enlarge control so visitors can switch between the metal part and the animation in the same space. The Roots blower already shares one period illustration across three stops, and the 190 E uses a Toyota axle to explain its suspension. Both patterns suit this tour. [Existing part images](../parts/) · [Photo interaction](../lib/app/story.js) · [190 E example](../stops/190e/car.js)
126	
127	| Stop and material | What to look for, then try in the animation |
128	| --- | --- |
129	| **1899 Daimler van · tubular radiator.** Crop Valder137’s original exhibit photograph around the round face and starting crank (CC BY 2.0). The outer face locates the cooler. Maybach’s 1897 sectional drawing shows what lies behind it. [Exhibit photograph](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Daimler_Motor-Gesch%C3%REDACTED%2814983294032%29.jpg) · [Maybach’s drawing](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tubular_car_radiator_copy_of_patent_drawing.png) | “Where does the air go after it enters the front of the radiator?” / „Merre áramlik tovább a levegő a hűtő belsejében?” Keep the starting crank visible as a landmark, then follow one air tube in section. Switch to the plain tank and see where air can reach its metal walls. |
130	| **300 SLR · desmodromic valves.** Gérard Delafond’s close-up looks through the inspection opening of a Ducati motorcycle engine. The upper rocker touches the valve tip and the fork beneath it catches the collar. CC BY-SA 3.0. [Ducati valve gear](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Desmo_photo.jpg) | “Which rocker pulls the valve shut?” / „Melyik himba húzza vissza a szelepet?” Mark the two contact points. Pause the Mercedes animation as the valve closes and find the contact that carries the load. The shared feature is mechanical closing. The Ducati photograph shows its own rocker layout. |
131	| **600 Pullman · hydraulic accumulator.** Nutzdatenbegleiter’s sectioned Citroën suspension sphere exposes the thick rubber diaphragm and the spaces on either side. CC BY-SA 4.0. [Citroën sphere in section](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cit-hydraulic-accumulator.jpg) | “What pushes the oil out while the pump is idle?” / „Mi nyomja ki az olajat, amikor a szivattyú áll?” Label gas, diaphragm and oil on the photo. Raise the 600’s rear window with the accumulator charged and watch the pressure drop. The Citroën uses the gas cushion in its suspension. The Mercedes uses stored pressure to move the window. |
132	
133	### Four more pairings with a specific job
134	
135	| Stop and image | Visitor prompt and model comparison |
136	| --- | --- |
137	| **260 D · diesel prechamber.** Gwafton’s photo shows a sectioned 1934 Ganz–Jendrassik diesel cylinder head. Credit the Hungarian engine by name and mark the small chamber and its outlet. CC BY-SA 3.0. [Cylinder-head section](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ganz-Jendrassik_combustion_chamber.JPG) | “Where does the fuel first burn?” / „Hol gyullad meg először a gázolaj?” Find the small chamber beside the cylinder, then follow the burning gases into the cylinder in the OM 138 animation. Use the donor to explain the two connected spaces. Their exact shapes differ between engines. |
138	| **300 SL Gullwing · straight-six crankshaft.** Dana60Cummins photographed a bare crankshaft laid beside its six-cylinder block. Keep the six bores and the full shaft in the crop. The source identifies the engine layout and leaves the vehicle unspecified. CC BY-SA 3.0. [Block and crankshaft](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:I6_Block_and_crankshaft.jpg) | “Which piston rises with piston 1?” / „Melyik dugattyú emelkedik együtt az elsővel?” Trace the first and last crank throws, then step the proposed balance animation to see pistons 1 and 6 rise together. The force arrows and torsional motion belong in the model. |
139	| **Benz Velo · belt selection.** Nick.Pr’s close-up of another 1894 Velo shows the two belt-control handles beside the driver. Keep both handles in the crop. CC0. [Velo driver’s controls](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Bench_seat_and_controls_of_Benz_Velo_of_1894.jpg) | “What moves under the seat when the driver moves a lever?” / „Mi mozdul el az ülés alatt, amikor a vezető átváltja a kart?” Start at the handles, then select a gear in the model and follow the belt sideways from the freely turning pulley onto the pulley fixed to the shaft. |
140	| **SLK · folding hardtop.** The side view of an R 170 SLK 230 catches the roof halfway into the boot. Crop around the rear of the cabin and keep the roof panel, rear window and raised boot lid together. Cerafino, CC BY-SA 2.5. [SLK roof mid-fold](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Slk_mb170_offen.jpg) | “Why does the boot lid open first?” / „Miért a csomagtérfedél nyílik ki először?” Match the model to the photograph, identify the gap the lid has opened, then continue the fold and see which panels pass through it. |
141	
142	**Caption and phone check.** Name the donor in the first sentence. For the Ducati photo, use “On this Ducati engine, the forked rocker pulls the valve shut by the collar on its stem.” / „Ennél a Ducati-motornál a villás himba a szelepszárra erősített gyűrűnél fogva húzza vissza a szelepet.” Keep the caption and alt text in both languages and credit the photographer, source, licence and any crop. In portrait view, a visitor should be able to point to the named feature in the enlarged photo and find it again in the model. Store the selected crops with the existing part images so the comparison also works offline.
143

# Museum tour wording and visitor experience

*Review of 25 November 2026, revision `636d7a4`. The review covered all 46 route cards in English and Hungarian. The route, highlights and selected exhibit interactions were checked in WebKit using iPhone 15 and iPad Pro 11 emulation. Gallery locations still need on-site confirmation.*

## Fix two obstacles on the visitor’s path

1. **Take visitors to the room picker.** Tapping “See the route” placed the first room at the top of the screen. The entire room picker was already above it on both devices. A visitor standing in Legend 6 would have to scroll backwards to discover the shortcut. Label the homepage button **Find your room** / **Teremválasztás** and link it to `#jump`. Point “See the full route” on the highlights page to `./#jump` as well. Check that following either link brings the room choices into view, including on a fresh page load. [Route](../index.html) · [Highlights](../teaser.html) · [Room picker](../lib/app/index.js)

2. **Make every SLK roof phase readable.** The Hungarian label *Csomagtartófedél fel* needed 112 px in a 76 px phone cell. It also overflowed the 81 px cell on the iPad in landscape. The prompt already identifies the boot lid, so the opening sequence can use **Fedél nyílik** and **Fedél zárul**. Use two columns when four labels cannot fit. Check the closing sequence too, so the highlighted wording describes the movement the visitor sees in either direction. [Roof controls](../subsystems/vario-roof.js) · [Hungarian labels](../lib/app/i18n/hu.js) · [Panel layout](../lib/app/theme.css)

## English and Hungarian copy

| Location | What gets in the way | Proposed English | Javasolt magyar szöveg |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 540 K route card | In “when did it join in?” and “mikor lépett működésbe?”, the nearest subject is the letter K. | What does the K stand for? When does the supercharger kick in? | Mit jelent a K betű? Mikor kapcsol be a kompresszor? |
| 300 SL frame comparison | “Lecsökkentve szokásos ajtókhoz” leaves out what was lowered. Visitors can see the sill change height. | Original high sill / Lower sill for conventional doors | Eredeti, magas küszöb / Alacsony küszöb hagyományos ajtóhoz |
| SLK roof prompt | “Watch the steps light up” draws attention to the indicators. In Hungarian, “a lépések kigyulladnak” can suggest catching fire. | Tap “Open the roof”. Which moves first, the boot lid or the roof? | Koppintson a „Tető nyitása” gombra. Mi mozdul meg először, a csomagtartó fedele vagy a tető? |
| Simplex gearbox legend | “Pair in mesh” leaves the parts unnamed. “Kapcsolódó kerékpár” can be read as a bicycle. | Gears in mesh | Kapcsolódó fogaskerekek |
| Offline instructions on the route and highlights | “With signal” and “térerővel” suggest mobile reception even on Wi-Fi. Opening the page starts the download. The ready message tells visitors when they can disconnect. | Open the tour while you’re online. When you see “Ready offline”, every stop is saved on this device. | Nyissa meg a túrát, amíg van internetkapcsolata. Amint az oldal jelzi, hogy a túra offline is elérhető, internet nélkül is megnyithatja bármelyik megállót. |
| Offline confirmation | “Offline is kész” sounds unfinished. Use the same wording in the instructions and the confirmation. | Ready offline. All stops are saved on this device. | A túra offline is elérhető. Az összes megálló mentve van a készüléken. |
| Benz Victoria route card | Both versions say the front wheels follow the same circle. The inner wheel follows a tighter arc, and the model shows the two steering angles. | Why does the inner front wheel turn more sharply? | Kanyarodáskor miért fordul el jobban a belső első kerék? |

The exhibit wording lives with the cars. Gear labels and offline messages are shared across pages. [540 K](../stops/540k/hu.js) · [300 SL](../stops/300sl/hu.js) · [SLK](../stops/slk/hu.js) · [Victoria](../stops/victoria/car.js) · [Gearbox](../subsystems/gearbox.js) · [Offline status](../lib/app/offline.js) · [Hungarian UI text](../lib/app/i18n/hu.js)

## Keep visitors oriented during an experiment

- **Preserve the comparison when switching languages.** On the 300 SL, selecting the lowered frame and switching languages restored the original frame and returned the page to the top. Someone looking up an unfamiliar term loses the example that explains it. Keep the active mechanism and selected setting in view. A practical check is to switch EN → HU → EN at the lowered frame and see the same comparison each time. [Language switch](../lib/app/i18n.js) · [Scroll story](../lib/app/story.js)
- **Give the other two highlights a question and a visual cue.** Three of the 46 route cards already pair a visitor question with something to find at the exhibit. The 300 SL does this well with its upward-opening doors and high sill. On the Blitzen-Benz, try **“If you double the power, do you double the speed?”** / **„Ha megduplázza a teljesítményt, a végsebesség is a kétszeresére nő?”** Have visitors compare the two speeds using the existing power slider. On the 300 SLR, invite them to raise the engine speed and watch where the spring-loaded valve stops following the cam. [Blitzen-Benz](../stops/blitzen-benz/car.js) · [300 SLR](../stops/300slr/car.js)

## Identify the exhibits accurately

**300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé.** The highlights introduction calls the exhibit the most expensive car ever sold. The stop itself correctly explains that Mercedes-Benz sold the other coupé. Use **“One of two Uhlenhaut Coupés. Its twin sold for €135 million in 2022.”** / **„A két Uhlenhaut Coupé egyike. A másik példány 2022-ben 135 millió euróért kelt el.”** [Highlights introduction](../teaser.html) · [Exhibit text](../stops/300slr/car.js) · [Mercedes-Benz sale announcement](https://group.mercedes-benz.com/company/news/uhlenhaut-coupe.html)

**O 302 football coach.** The route card, photo description and exhibit text identify the displayed vehicle as the coach that carried the team. Daimler Truck identifies it as a replica. Use **“A replica of West Germany’s 1974 World Cup team bus”** / **„A nyugatnémet válogatott 1974-es világbajnoki csapatbuszának másolata”** wherever visitors first encounter it. Verify the room separately. The tour lists Collection 1, while Daimler Truck’s 2022 exhibit photographs are captioned Collection 4. [English exhibit text](../stops/o302/car.js) · [Hungarian exhibit text](../stops/o302/hu.js) · [Route placement](../stops/tour.js) · [Daimler Truck exhibit description and photographs](https://www.daimlertruck.com/en/newsroom/pressrelease/maximum-bus-comfort-for-the-1974-world-cup-footballers-52102483)

## Evolution II — put the racing bodywork in the wind tunnel

Klaus Ludwig’s number 3 DTM car is the reason to open this stop. The visitor can pick out the wing above the boot, the lip below the front bumper and the flared arches around the tyres in the exhibit photo. Yet both body buttons feed **the same solid shape** to the flow solver. The wing appears in the outline but is omitted from the CFD profile, the underside is flat, and the wheels lie outside the centre plane. Switching bodies changes the road-car drag and top-speed calculation. It cannot show what those three parts do to the air. Move the autobahn comparison into the background as road-car context. [Exhibit photo](../stops/190e-evo2/photo.jpg) · [Evo II configuration](../stops/190e-evo2/car.js) · [How the tunnel is selected](../subsystems/aero.js)

**Open at a fast corner.** Ask **“Why would a racing driver accept more drag?”** / **„Miért éri meg a versenyzőnek a nagyobb légellenállás?”** Start at one fixed speed with the wing selected. Highlight the part on the photo, then show the same part close up in the flow. One tap changes one piece of geometry. Keep the camera, speed and colour scale fixed so the visitor can see what changed.

| Part and visitor action | What to reveal in the CFD | What it means on track |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Rear wing · Hátsó szárny.** Extend the adjustable upper flap. Keep the lower strip and roof-edge spoiler fixed. | Show the pressure on both wing surfaces, the flow arriving from the rear window, and the wake. Put a downward arrow at the wing and a rearward arrow for drag. Let their lengths follow the calculated forces. | Extra rear aerodynamic load can give the rear tyres more grip in a fast bend. Extra drag costs speed on the following straight. The two arrows make the price of the adjustment visible. |
| **Front splitter · Első légterelő lemez.** Switch the front lip between its two longitudinal positions. | Zoom to the nose at road level. Show where air meets the upper face and where it passes under the lip. Compare the change in front aerodynamic load alongside rear load, with the wing setting held fixed. | A driver needs the front tyres to turn the car as well as the rears to hold their line. Moving aerodynamic load forward can help when the front runs wide in a fast bend. |
| **Flared fender · Kiszélesített sárvédő.** Compare the flared arch with a reference contour that clears the same tyre. Label the reference as an experiment. | Use a view across the front wheel and a velocity slice just behind it. Trace the flow that passes around the tyre shoulder and rejoins the body side. Hold tyre width, wheel position, rotation and ride height fixed. | The flare accommodates the wheel. Its shape also changes the disturbed air the rest of the car encounters. Let the measured change in this model determine what the caption says about drag. |

The FIA’s Evo II homologation extension **A-5269, 29/02 ES**, sheets 5–7, gives photographs and drawings of the front lip, upper and lower rear flaps, roof-edge spoiler and cylinder head. Use them with the number 3 photo to establish geometry. Mercedes-Benz documents the front lip’s two positions and the extendable upper flap on the homologation car. Identify the proposed settings as comparisons wherever the 1992 race setup is unknown. Wheel-arch experiments also show why the wheel position must be controlled when comparing fenders. [FIA Group A homologation form](https://historicdb.fia.com/sites/default/files/car_attachment/1601062201/homologation_form_number_5269_group_a.pdf) · [Mercedes-Benz on the adjustable aero package](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/4e61dcd8-fd75-47ca-830c-056734a165c2) · [Rotating-wheel and wheelhouse experiment](https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1073/12/17/3340)

**Compute four cases ahead of time.** For this stop, use one simplified 3D car, a moving road and rotating wheels. Solve a baseline plus one change per part. Export just the pressure and velocity slices, a few streamlines and mean force differences for the existing stage to display offline. The fender needs lateral flow, which the live side-view solver cannot resolve. For front and rear load, derive the axle reactions from the whole-body vertical force and pitching moment about a known reference. The force on the wing alone does not give the rear axle load. Show relative changes in the exhibit and identify them as results for the simplified model. [Existing flow solver](../lib/model/flow.js) · [Wind-tunnel rendering](../lib/scene/wind-tunnel.js)

**Pilot the wing first.** Resolve the flap and its gap in the computational mesh. Check that the direction of the averaged load and drag changes survives mesh refinement before writing the takeaway. Repeat that check for the lip and fender. If the fender’s drag difference is smaller than the numerical uncertainty, show the change in its wake and leave the drag delta unreported. On an offline iPhone, each switch should reveal a visible difference at the selected part, with a text description that also works with motion reduced. A visitor should be able to explain why a team might choose different settings for two circuits.

## Evolution II — give the racing engine one short experiment

**Yes, the 2.5-litre four is worth a second step.** It earns its place by showing how little time a racing cylinder has to fill. Mercedes-Benz specifies a 97.8 mm bore and 82.8 mm stroke for the race engine. The early DTM version produced 245 kW at 8,500 rpm and could reach 9,500 rpm. The figure quoted for the 1992 championship car is **up to 274 kW (373 PS)**. The road Evo II had a 97.3 mm bore and produced 173 kW (235 PS). Keep each power figure attached to its version. The source gives the early engine’s maximum speed separately from the 1992 power figure. [Mercedes-Benz on the road and race engines](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/25dd00e4-5ef9-4c2f-b12c-55169f795d4d)

Ask **“At 9,000 rpm, how long does one cylinder have for its intake stroke?”** / **„Percenként 9000-es fordulatszámnál hány ezredmásodpercig tart a szívóütem?”** Let the visitor switch between 4,500 and 9,000 rpm while watching one cylinder in slow motion. The crank turns through the intake stroke in **6.7 ms and 3.3 ms** respectively. Highlight the two inlet valves opening together as the piston descends. Freeze the view from above so the visitor can see both inlet openings available to fill the cylinder in that brief interval. In the side view, the short stroke means the piston travels less distance per revolution at a given engine speed. Put the real elapsed time beside the picture. These times describe 180° of crank rotation. Actual valve opening extends over a different interval determined by cam timing.

Reuse the four-stroke animation and show **two camshafts and four valves per cylinder** before inviting visitors to count them. The current generic DOHC view draws one inlet and one exhaust valve per cylinder. The FIA head photograph on sheet 7 gives the model a visual reference. Use a slow-motion time scale and a pause control so visitors can follow one cam revolution through two crank revolutions. Put power figures in the supporting text. The useful result of the experiment is the time available to breathe. [Engine renderer](../subsystems/inline-engine.js) · [Four-stroke timing](../lib/model/engine.js) · [FIA cylinder-head photograph, extension 29/02 ES](https://historicdb.fia.com/sites/default/files/car_attachment/1601062201/homologation_form_number_5269_group_a.pdf)

## Camshafts — match each explanation to the engine on screen

The shared piston-engine panel always creates and updates a **Camshaft / Vezérműtengely** angle by dividing crank angle by two. Six of its 19 configured engines draw no separate camshaft. Other stops do draw a shaft but leave out the link to the valve. These cases need different edits. [Panel, drawing and update logic](../subsystems/inline-engine.js)

| Stops | What the model and text say today | Proposed correction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Benz Patent-Motorwagen | The valve gear is omitted in the drawing. A camshaft angle still runs. Mercedes-Benz describes an intake slide and a controlled exhaust valve on the real engine. | Remove the camshaft readout and its per-frame update for this view. Keep the crank angle. Describe the pictured piston and flywheel, and identify any discussion of the actual valve gear as background. [Stop configuration](../stops/patent-motorwagen/car.js) · [Mercedes-Benz on the original engine](https://group.mercedes-benz.com/company/tradition/company-history/1885-1886.html) |
| Daimler stationary engine, Reitwagen, motor carriage, Marie motorboat and Benz Velo | All five use the atmospheric-inlet drawing. It shows a moving exhaust rod and a suction-operated inlet. The panel labels a separate half-speed shaft. The Daimler engine story describes a groove driving the exhaust. | Show the intake opening as the piston descends. For the documented Daimler drive, highlight the groove, follower and exhaust rod when those parts are depicted. Verify the exhaust drive for each variant, especially the Benz Velo, before reusing that description. Use the crank or stroke indicator for timing. [Daimler engine stop](../stops/daimler-engine/car.js) · [Velo stop](../stops/velo/car.js) · [Mercedes-Benz on the Daimler exhaust drive](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/article/f37c559a-5986-4a7a-ab64-6fc195752b99) |
| 190 SL and engines with visible shafts | The 190 SL introduction says the cam opens the valve “directly”. The factory workshop manual shows a rocker arm between the cam and valve. The shared overhead-cam drawing leaves that rocker out. At the Simplex 60 stop, the text itself records that its side exhaust valve is drawn overhead. | Correct the 190 SL wording in both languages and show one complete cam–rocker–valve path in close-up. On the Simplex 60, focus on the documented overhead inlet and distinguish the side exhaust in the cutaway. At other shaft-equipped stops, check the default view for the part the visitor is asked to watch. [190 SL wording](../stops/190sl/car.js) · [Workshop manual, fig. 01-4/20a](https://s3cf792cad773e861.jimcontent.com/download/version/1612462948/module/15676396822/name/Mercedes%20Benz%20Service%20Manual%20180%20to%20220SE.pdf) · [Simplex 60 geometry note](../stops/simplex-60/car.js) |

Use the same valvetrain configuration to draw the shaft, show its readout and update its angle. For the Daimler engine, use **“Watch the inlet open as the piston moves down.”** / **„Figyelje meg, hogyan nyílik ki a szívószelep, amikor a dugattyú lefelé indul.”** For the corrected 190 SL cutaway, use **“Follow the cam as it presses the rocker arm and opens the valve.”** / **„Figyelje meg, hogyan nyomja le a bütyök a szelephimbát, és hogyan nyílik ki a szelep.”**

Check all 19 configurations for agreement between the drawing, readout and both languages. Exercise at least one view each with omitted gear, atmospheric inlet, pushrods, a single overhead cam and twin overhead cams. A shaft-equipped model should show one shaft revolution per two crank revolutions. In a view with omitted gear the crank and piston should still run with the cam readout absent. For every “watch” prompt, pause at the opening stroke on a phone and check that the named part and what it moves are both identifiable.

## 260 D (W 138) — refit the body outline to the exhibit photo

The outline extends well beyond the rear of the black Pullman saloon. On the 1200 × 803 photo, the current camera projects the near-side lower rear corner to roughly (78, 400), more than 200 pixels to the left of the car at that height. The fit uses the right front wheel and estimated headlamp and grille positions. It has no rear-axle landmark to check how the length of the car projects into the distance. [Exhibit photo](../stops/260d/photo.jpg) · [Body outline and camera](../stops/260d/car.js) · [Camera-fit landmarks](../tools/photo-fits/260d.json)

Refit the camera using the front and rear road wheels of the photographed Pullman. Take care to distinguish the side-mounted spare from the rear road wheel. If the rear hub is too obscured to place reliably, use a clearer side or three-quarter photograph of the same body variant to establish its proportions. With the perspective checked, trace the bonnet, windscreen, roof and rear body at their respective widths. Also reconcile the wheel outline’s 400 mm outer radius with the 360 mm axle height used in the fit.

**Acceptance check.** Compare the old and revised outlines over the original photo. The wheel outlines should follow the visible tyres, the roof and rear corners should follow the black saloon, and the engine overlay should sit beneath its bonnet. Use roof and body landmarks held out of the camera fit for this check, then inspect the closing photo step on iPhone and iPad. [Photo-overlay tool](../tools/photo-grid.mjs) · [Profile tracing tool](../tools/trace-profile.mjs)

## W 196 R — follow the air behind the front wheel

Switching between the open-wheel car and the streamliner changes the assumed drag, frontal area and mass in the straight-line calculation. Both buttons select the same centre-plane profile for the wind tunnel. Comparing the two 218 × 64 grids gives **zero differing solid cells**. The plane passes between the wheels, so the airflow where the bodywork changes is missing from the experiment. [W 196 R configurations](../stops/w196r/car.js) · [Tunnel selection](../subsystems/aero.js)

**Visitor question.** “What happens to the air behind the front tyre when the bodywork covers it?” / „Hogyan változik a légáramlás az első kerék mögött, ha burkolat kerül fölé?” Start with a front three-quarter view. Let visitors switch between **Open wheels / Szabadon álló kerekek** and **Streamlined body / Áramvonalas karosszéria**. Switch the visible body and the flow field together. Keep a few streamlines seeded just ahead of the front tyre and a fixed, wheel-height slice extending past the rear wheel. A speed map shows where the air slows in the wake and how far that wake extends alongside the car.

Use the offline 3D CFD approach proposed for the Evo II. Compute the two complete body shapes at equal speed, ride height, yaw and wheel rotation over a moving road. Compare them with the same camera, seed positions and colour scale. Report the mean drag change for the **whole body style**, since enclosing the wheels also changes the car’s width and flanks. The existing “about 20 km/h” belongs with the illustrative straight-line calculation. Finish by switching to the driver’s view. At Monza the streamlined body suited the fast circuit. On winding tracks the exposed front wheels let the driver judge where to place the car. [1955 streamliner](https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/Mercedes-Benz-W-196-R-streamlined-racing-car-1955.xhtml?oid=6877) · [Mercedes-Benz on the driver’s view](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/b210a620-ecd7-42dc-b364-af3e85ff3d6c)

**Acceptance check.** At a fixed speed, pause and toggle the body. The exposed front tread should give way to the fairing in the oncoming stream, and the wheel-height field should show a repeatable wake difference with the scale held fixed. Verify that difference against a refined mesh. A visitor should be able to point to it on a phone in either language, including offline and with animation paused.

## Straight-sixes and straight-eights — why a smooth engine can still twist its crankshaft

Give the **300 SL** the balance experiment, the **770** the firing-pulse comparison and the **W 196 R** the historical engineering decision. The moving pistons exert reactions on the engine block and its mounts. Within each cylinder, the primary inertia force repeats once per crank revolution. The connecting rod’s changing angle introduces a secondary component that repeats twice. In the tour’s symmetric, equal-mass six- and eight-cylinder layouts, the first- and second-order forces and their rocking moments cancel in the sum. The crankshaft still receives torque pulses at different positions along its length, and the driveline carries the resulting fluctuating torque. [Engine kinematics](../lib/model/engine.js) · [Reciprocating forces and engine balance](https://www.epi-eng.com/piston_engine_technology/forces_on_recip_components.htm)

| Stop | What the visitor does and sees | Discussion prompt |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **300 SL Gullwing · Straight-six balance** | Pause the existing engine and step through a revolution. Show a force arrow along each cylinder, then their sum and the rocking moment about the engine midpoint. Pistons 1 and 6 move together. Add the other two pairs and watch the total cancel. Switch between the once-per-revolution and twice-per-revolution components. The 190 E’s conventional inline-four makes a useful comparison because its secondary forces add. | “How can six moving pistons leave the engine balanced?” / „Hogyan egyenlítik ki egymás tehetetlenségi erőit a soros hathengeres dugattyúi?” |
| **770 · Straight-eight firing pulses** | Keep the existing firing animation and put a torque trace at the crank output. At the same 3,000 rpm, an evenly firing four-stroke six has three firing pulses per revolution (150 per second), and an evenly firing eight has four (200 per second). Highlight each firing cylinder as its pulse reaches the trace. Compare at equal mean torque so visitors can distinguish pulse spacing from engine power. | “Can you still pick out the individual power strokes at the output?” / „A főtengelyen leadott nyomaték görbéjén felismerhetők az egyes munkaütemek?” |
| **W 196 R · Crankshaft resonance** | After the aero story, show the two groups of four cylinders and the gear that takes power from the middle of the crankshaft. Mark the front, centre and rear of the shaft with witness lines. Sweep engine rpm and watch the relative twist grow near a torsional natural frequency. Let visitors compare the actual centre take-off with an illustrative end take-off under the same firing input and load. Trace the torque path to the propeller shaft and rear transaxle. | “Why did Mercedes take the drive from the middle of the crankshaft?” / „Miért a főtengely közepéről hajtották meg a hátsó kerekeket?” |

The W 196 R makes the distinction tangible. Taking power from the middle gives each four-cylinder group a shorter path to the output gear. Mercedes-Benz records vibration as a reason for that choice. Resonance is a separate observation in the model: when a repeated torque input excites a natural twisting mode, the relative angle can grow even while the engine remains externally balanced. Offer a damping control to see the resonance peak diminish. Label it as a model experiment. [300 SL engine](../stops/300sl/car.js) · [770 engine](../stops/770/car.js) · [Mercedes-Benz archive on the M 196 centre drive](https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/Mercedes-Benz-W-196-R-streamlined-racing-car-1954.xhtml?oid=6873) · [Measured six-cylinder crankshaft response with and without a damper](https://saemobilus.sae.org/papers/experiment-computation-analyses-torsional-vibration-crankshaft-system-viscous-torsional-damper-diesel-engine-1999-01-1748)

**Model and proof.** Reuse the existing crank angles, cylinder positions, stroke and rod length for the balance arrows. Use real rpm for the calculations and slow motion for the picture. For torsion, connect front, centre and rear crank inertias with elastic, damped segments and couple the chosen output to a driveline load. Plot relative angle along the **crankshaft / főtengely** and transmitted torque in the **propeller shaft / kardántengely**. Mark exaggerated twist, assumed stiffness, damping, inertias and firing inputs as illustrative. Exact M 196 firing phases and critical speeds need period evidence before they can be attributed to the car.

Check the force and moment sums through a full revolution, and check pulse counts across a full 720° firing cycle. In the torsion model, hold excitation amplitude fixed and compare steady-state twist below, near and above resonance, then repeat with more damping. A visitor should be able to pause on a balanced force display and a fluctuating torque trace and explain why both can be true.

## 1899 Daimler motorised business vehicle — what flows through the radiator tubes?

Start on the photograph. Highlight the round radiator below the engine and use the starting crank through its centre as a landmark. Zoom into one tube and ask “What flows through this tube, water or air?” / „Mi áramlik a cső belsejében, víz vagy levegő?” The current animation sends air particles along the same straight paths for both designs, which makes the solid tank look as though air can pass through it too. [Museum description of the van](https://media.mercedes-benz.fr/lancetre-des-sprinter--co-lutilitaire-motorise-daimler-de-1899/) · [Current animation](../subsystems/radiator.js)

| Visitor choice | What the cutaway should show |
| --- | --- |
| **Maybach’s tubular radiator / Maybach csöves hűtője** · fitted to the van | Follow an air arrow through an open tube. Water from the engine flows around the outside of the tube. Highlight the thin metal wall where heat passes from water to air, then pull back to reveal the many tubes. Each adds surface through which the passing air can carry heat away. [Mercedes-Benz Classic on the two flow paths](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/08562e56-d477-4fc4-8f64-7a616cf18189) |
| **Plain water tank / Egyszerű víztartály** · illustrative comparison | Keep the same viewpoint. Air divides around the closed tank. Highlight its outer walls as the surface through which it sheds heat. The water stores the excess heat and its temperature rises. |

Give the comparison one repeatable starting point. Start both systems with 90 °C water, at 16 km/h and 60% engine load. Ask “In which system will the water cool down as you drive?” / „Melyik rendszerben hűl le a víz menet közben?” With the stop’s illustrative settings, the engine adds 3.6 kW to the water. At first the tank sheds about 1.5 kW and the radiator sheds 4.2 kW. Show the two temperature traces on a shared clock. The tank reaches boiling while the radiator settles at 80 °C. Visitors can then change speed or load and try their prediction again. [Van settings](../stops/daimler-van/car.js) · [Cooling model](../lib/model/cooling.js)

**Acceptance check.** On a phone, pause the cutaway in either language. A visitor should be able to trace the labelled water and air paths without relying on colour, point to the surface that carries heat between them, and identify which design the van used. Replaying the comparison should restore both starting temperatures and reproduce both curves.

## Real parts beside the animations

Start with the **Daimler van, 300 SLR and 600 Pullman**. Each photograph answers a question the moving model leaves open. Use the tour’s existing tap-to-enlarge control so visitors can switch between the metal part and the animation in the same space. The Roots blower already shares one period illustration across three stops, and the 190 E uses a Toyota axle to explain its suspension. Both patterns suit this tour. [Existing part images](../parts/) · [Photo interaction](../lib/app/story.js) · [190 E example](../stops/190e/car.js)

| Stop and material | What to look for, then try in the animation |
| --- | --- |
| **1899 Daimler van · tubular radiator.** Crop Valder137’s original exhibit photograph around the round face and starting crank (CC BY 2.0). The outer face locates the cooler. Maybach’s 1897 sectional drawing shows what lies behind it. [Exhibit photograph](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Daimler_Motor-Gesch%C3%REDACTED%2814983294032%29.jpg) · [Maybach’s drawing](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tubular_car_radiator_copy_of_patent_drawing.png) | “Where does the air go after it enters the front of the radiator?” / „Merre áramlik tovább a levegő a hűtő belsejében?” Keep the starting crank visible as a landmark, then follow one air tube in section. Switch to the plain tank and see where air can reach its metal walls. |
| **300 SLR · desmodromic valves.** Gérard Delafond’s close-up looks through the inspection opening of a Ducati motorcycle engine. The upper rocker touches the valve tip and the fork beneath it catches the collar. CC BY-SA 3.0. [Ducati valve gear](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Desmo_photo.jpg) | “Which rocker pulls the valve shut?” / „Melyik himba húzza vissza a szelepet?” Mark the two contact points. Pause the Mercedes animation as the valve closes and find the contact that carries the load. The shared feature is mechanical closing. The Ducati photograph shows its own rocker layout. |
| **600 Pullman · hydraulic accumulator.** Nutzdatenbegleiter’s sectioned Citroën suspension sphere exposes the thick rubber diaphragm and the spaces on either side. CC BY-SA 4.0. [Citroën sphere in section](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cit-hydraulic-accumulator.jpg) | “What pushes the oil out while the pump is idle?” / „Mi nyomja ki az olajat, amikor a szivattyú áll?” Label gas, diaphragm and oil on the photo. Raise the 600’s rear window with the accumulator charged and watch the pressure drop. The Citroën uses the gas cushion in its suspension. The Mercedes uses stored pressure to move the window. |

### Four more pairings with a specific job

| Stop and image | Visitor prompt and model comparison |
| --- | --- |
| **260 D · diesel prechamber.** Gwafton’s photo shows a sectioned 1934 Ganz–Jendrassik diesel cylinder head. Credit the Hungarian engine by name and mark the small chamber and its outlet. CC BY-SA 3.0. [Cylinder-head section](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ganz-Jendrassik_combustion_chamber.JPG) | “Where does the fuel first burn?” / „Hol gyullad meg először a gázolaj?” Find the small chamber beside the cylinder, then follow the burning gases into the cylinder in the OM 138 animation. Use the donor to explain the two connected spaces. Their exact shapes differ between engines. |
| **300 SL Gullwing · straight-six crankshaft.** Dana60Cummins photographed a bare crankshaft laid beside its six-cylinder block. Keep the six bores and the full shaft in the crop. The source identifies the engine layout and leaves the vehicle unspecified. CC BY-SA 3.0. [Block and crankshaft](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:I6_Block_and_crankshaft.jpg) | “Which piston rises with piston 1?” / „Melyik dugattyú emelkedik együtt az elsővel?” Trace the first and last crank throws, then step the proposed balance animation to see pistons 1 and 6 rise together. The force arrows and torsional motion belong in the model. |
| **Benz Velo · belt selection.** Nick.Pr’s close-up of another 1894 Velo shows the two belt-control handles beside the driver. Keep both handles in the crop. CC0. [Velo driver’s controls](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Bench_seat_and_controls_of_Benz_Velo_of_1894.jpg) | “What moves under the seat when the driver moves a lever?” / „Mi mozdul el az ülés alatt, amikor a vezető átváltja a kart?” Start at the handles, then select a gear in the model and follow the belt sideways from the freely turning pulley onto the pulley fixed to the shaft. |
| **SLK · folding hardtop.** The side view of an R 170 SLK 230 catches the roof halfway into the boot. Crop around the rear of the cabin and keep the roof panel, rear window and raised boot lid together. Cerafino, CC BY-SA 2.5. [SLK roof mid-fold](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Slk_mb170_offen.jpg) | “Why does the boot lid open first?” / „Miért a csomagtérfedél nyílik ki először?” Match the model to the photograph, identify the gap the lid has opened, then continue the fold and see which panels pass through it. |

**Caption and phone check.** Name the donor in the first sentence. For the Ducati photo, use “On this Ducati engine, the forked rocker pulls the valve shut by the collar on its stem.” / „Ennél a Ducati-motornál a villás himba a szelepszárra erősített gyűrűnél fogva húzza vissza a szelepet.” Keep the caption and alt text in both languages and credit the photographer, source, licence and any crop. In portrait view, a visitor should be able to point to the named feature in the enlarged photo and find it again in the model. Store the selected crops with the existing part images so the comparison also works offline.
