content.content:
--- 2026-11-25T17:43:07.548Z Everything passes: 229 unit tests and 277 e2e (the 144 skipped are the Hungarian pass, which runs on iPhone only by design). Last, a CLAUDE.md "Open" note for the O 302 room question.
--- 2026-11-25T17:52:41.211Z Now the camshaft audit: listing every engine configuration's valve gear and its prompts.
--- 2026-11-25T17:53:29.944Z Six of the 19 engines draw no camshaft (Patent-Motorwagen plus the five atmospheric-inlet engines), matching the proposal. Checking the valve-lift model and the Evo II stop next.
--- 2026-11-25T18:28:33.581Z The simulations are still running. Meanwhile I'm refitting the 260 D photo camera from both of its road wheels. Looking at the photo now.
--- 2026-11-25T18:32:23.823Z The 260 D refit lines up: the front tyre, grille, bonnet, roof and the visible rear now sit on the car. Checking how far the CFD runs have got:
--- 2026-11-25T18:37:41.922Z The engines draw correctly. The Evo II's top view hides the inlet valves under the camshafts, so I'm tilting that view a little toward the side.
--- 2026-11-25T19:12:31.779Z Still running: the 28 mm wind-tunnel runs need about 40 more minutes. Nothing is committed or pushed.

**Done since the last update**
- **CFD runs:** the tunnel runs offline on 10 cores, with the wheels held still (spinning tyres on the block-shaped cells pumped air through the model). Each case is computed on a 40 mm and a 28 mm grid.
- **Forces:** I now take drag, lift and the load on each axle from the pressure on the car's surface. The solver's own force sum matched that in the changes between cases but put the flap's effect on the wrong axle, so it now only serves as the noise estimate. Friction is left out, which is fine for showing the idea.
- **40 mm results:**
  - The raised flap adds rear downforce (+0.12 in coefficient, about 50 kg at 200 km/h) and costs drag (+0.08), with the front slightly lighter. That is what a wing should do.

The search confirmed the bore, stroke, and incline, but not the firing order.

- **Bore and stroke:** The M 196 R's 76 mm bore and 68.8 mm stroke are confirmed by several sources, including a [Wikipedia-mirror entry](https://wiki.riteme.site/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_M196_engine) and a [technical specification page](https://www.f1technical.net/forum/viewtopic.php?p=808994). Its displacement is about 2.5 litres.
- **Incline:** One Wikipedia-based source says the M 196 S is canted to the right at a 53° angle. That source does not give the same figure for the R version, so the 53° is confirmed only for the S.
- **Central take-off:** A [Wikiwand mirror](https://wikiwand.com/en/articles/Mercedes-Benz_M196_engine) describes the crankshaft of the S, not the R, as consisting of two Hirth joint halves with centre torque take-off.
- **Bore/stroke variant:** The S version used 78 × 78 mm, per the [Wikipedia entry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_M196_engine), so the S and R should not be mixed up.
- **Firing order:** No result gave the M 196's firing order. A [forum thread](https://forums.autosport.com/topic/217186-mercedes-benz-m196r-m196s-engines) on the M 196 R and S notes the bore and stroke difference but not the firing order. Another [forum thread](https://forums.autosport.com/topic/35281-straight-eight) says the M 196 must have had unusual exhaust manifolding, but it gives no sequence. A further search aimed at period technical sources or enthusiast documentation would be needed for the firing order.

lines: // Air temperature at the end of compression (°C), polytropic: T₂ = T₁ · ε^(n − 1). Real engines lose heat to the walls,
// so n ≈ 1.3 rather than the adiabatic 1.4.
export const compressionTemp = (ratio, t1 = 20, n = 1.3) => (t1 + 273.15) * ratio ** (n - 1) - 273.15;
+// Shaking forces (docs/bilingual-copy-and-ux-proposals.md, straight-six balance). Each piston's inertia pushes on the block
+// along its cylinder (+ = away from the crank), in units of m·r·ω²: first order cos α, once per turn; second order
+// λ·cos 2α with λ = r/l, twice per turn, from the conrod's changing angle. Summed over an inline engine at crank angle θ,
+// with the rocking moment about the middle of the block (xs in any length unit; moment in that unit × m·r·ω²).
+export const inertiaForce = (alpha, lambda, order) => (order === 1 ? Math.cos(alpha) : lambda * Math.cos(2 * alpha));
+export function shaking(lay, theta, xs, lambda, order) {
+  const xc = (Math.min(...xs) + Math.max(...xs)) / 2, f = xs.map((_, i) => inertiaForce(theta + lay.throwA[i], lambda, order));
+  return { f, sum: f.reduce((a, v) => a + v, 0), moment: f.reduce((a, v, i) => a + v * (xs[i] - xc), 0) };
+// Crank torque from gas pressure, illustrative: over its 720° cycle each cylinder pushes during the power stroke (strong
+// just after firing, fading as the gas expands) and drags a little while it compresses. crankTorque sums the cylinders at
+// crank angle θ and scales so its mean is 1: engines compare at equal mean torque, which keeps pulse spacing apart from power.
+const gasPulse = ph => (ph < Math.PI ? Math.sin(ph) * (1 - ph / Math.PI) ** 1.5 : ph > 3 * Math.PI ? -0.25 * Math.sin(ph - 3 * Math.PI) * (ph - 3 * Math.PI) / Math.PI : 0);
+const PULSE_MEAN = (() => { let s = 0; const N = 7200; for (let k = 0; k < N; k++) s += gasPulse((k + 0.5) / N * CYCLE); return s / N; })();
+export const crankTorque = (lay, theta) => lay.offset.reduce((a, o) => a + gasPulse(phaseOf(theta, o)), 0) / (lay.n * PULSE_MEAN);
+// Power strokes per crank revolution and per second for an evenly firing four-stroke.
+export const pulsesPerTurn = n => n / 2;
+export const pulsesPerSecond = (n, rpm) => n / 2 * rpm / 60;
+// Crankshaft twist (torsional vibration), illustrative: the crank of a straight-eight as two lumped halves (cylinders 1–4
+// and 5–8), elastic between them, with the output gear either in the middle (the M 196's centre take-off) or behind the
+// last cylinder (an end take-off for comparison). The gear drives a heavy driveline through a soft propeller shaft.
+// Each half receives the same torque ripple at the firing frequency (four pulses per crank turn); damping is structural
+// (stiffness k(1 + 2iζ)), so a resonance peak scales as 1 / 2ζ. Steady-state response by a complex linear solve. Pure.
+// Positions along the crank as a share of its length: halves at ¼ and ¾, the gear at ½ or 1.
+export const TORSION = { J: 0.02, Jgear: 0.01, Jload: 0.3, K: 1.2e4, kProp: 3000, ripple: 0.6, order: 4 };   // all illustrative
+export function torsionResponse(layout, rpm, zeta, p = TORSION) {
+  const gearAt = layout === "centre" ? 0.5 : 1, nodes = [{ x: 0.25, J: p.J, T: 1 }, { x: 0.75, J: p.J, T: 1 }, { x: gearAt, J: p.Jgear, T: 0, gear: true }].sort((a, b) => a.x - b.x);
+  nodes.push({ J: p.Jload, T: 0, load: true });
+  const n = nodes.length, w = p.order * rpm / 60 * 2 * Math.PI, g = nodes.findIndex(q => q.gear);
+  // Springs: neighbours along the crank (stiffness ∝ 1 / length), and the gear to the load.
+  const springs = [];
+  for (let i = 0; i < n - 2; i++) springs.push([i, i + 1, p.K / (nodes[i + 1].x - nodes[i].x)]);
+  springs.push([g, n - 1, p.kProp]);
+  // (K* − ω² J) θ = T, complex as [re, im] pairs.
+  const A = Array.from({ length: n }, () => Array.from({ length: n }, () => [0, 0])), b = nodes.map(q => [q.T, 0]);
+  for (const [i, j, k] of springs) for (const [a, c, s] of [[i, i, 1], [j, j, 1], [i, j, -1], [j, i, -1]]) { A[a][c][0] += s * k; A[a][c][1] += s * k * 2 * zeta; }
+  nodes.forEach((q, i) => (A[i][i][0] -= w * w * q.J));
+  const th = solve(A, b), amp = ([re, im]) => Math.hypot(re, im), sub = (u, v) => [u[0] - v[0], u[1] - v[1]];
+  // Twist: the larger swing of either crank half against the gear; propeller-shaft torque swing per unit ripple.
+  const halves = nodes.map((q, i) => i).filter(i => i !== g && !nodes[i].load);
+  return { twist: Math.max(...halves.map(i => amp(sub(th[i], th[g])))), prop: amp(sub(th[g], th[n - 1])) * p.kProp,
+    nodes: nodes.map((q, i) => ({ x: q.x, gear: !!q.gear, load: !!q.load, rel: sub(th[i], th[g]) })) };
+// Engine speed (rpm) where the twist peaks, searched over [lo, hi].
+export function resonanceRpm(layout, zeta, lo = 1000, hi = 12000, p = TORSION) {
+  let best = lo, max = -1;
+  for (let r = lo; r <= hi; r += 25) { const v = torsionResponse(layout, r, zeta, p).twist; if (v > max) { max = v; best = r; } }
+  return max > 1.5 * torsionResponse(layout, hi, zeta, p).twist && best < hi ? best : null;   // null: no peak inside the range
+function solve(A, b) {   // Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting, complex entries [re, im]

+import { test } from "node:test";
+import assert from "node:assert/strict";
+import { layout, shaking, crankTorque, pulsesPerTurn, pulsesPerSecond } from "../../lib/model/engine.js";
+import { torsionResponse, resonanceRpm } from "../../lib/model/torsion.js";
+const TAU = 2 * Math.PI, turn = f => Array.from({ length: 72 }, (_, k) => f(k / 72 * TAU));
+const six = layout([1, 5, 3, 6, 2, 4]), four = layout([1, 3, 4, 2]), eight = layout([1, 6, 2, 5, 8, 3, 7, 4]);
+test("straight-six: first- and second-order forces and rocking moments cancel through a revolution", () => {
+  for (const order of [1, 2]) turn(th => {
+    const s = shaking(six, th, xs6, lambda, order);
+    assert.ok(Math.abs(s.sum) < 1e-9 && Math.abs(s.moment) < 1e-9, `order ${order} at ${th}`);
+test("inline four: first order cancels, second-order forces add (4λ cos 2θ)", () => {
+  turn(th => {
+    assert.ok(Math.abs(shaking(four, th, xs4, lambda, 1).sum) < 1e-9);
+    assert.ok(Math.abs(shaking(four, th, xs4, lambda, 2).sum - 4 * lambda * Math.cos(2 * th)) < 1e-9);
+test("firing pulses: equal mean torque; the eight's swing is smaller; pulse counts at 3,000 rpm", () => {

+  const stats = lay => { const v = Array.from({ length: 1440 }, (_, k) => crankTorque(lay, k / 1440 * 2 * TAU)); return { mean: v.reduce((a, b) => a + b) / v.length, swing: Math.max(...v) - Math.min(...v) }; };
+  const s6 = stats(six), s8 = stats(eight);
+  assert.ok(Math.abs(s6.mean - 1) < 1e-3 && Math.abs(s8.mean - 1) < 1e-3);
+  assert.ok(s8.swing < s6.swing);
+  assert.equal(pulsesPerTurn(6), 3); assert.equal(pulsesPerTurn(8), 4);
+  assert.equal(pulsesPerSecond(6, 3000), 150); assert.equal(pulsesPerSecond(8, 3000), 200);
+test("crank twist: the end take-off resonates inside the rev range, the centre take-off does not; damping lowers the peak", () => {
+  assert.equal(resonanceRpm("centre", 0.03, 1000, 9000), null);
+  const r = resonanceRpm("end", 0.03, 1000, 9000);
+  assert.ok(r > 5000 && r < 8000, String(r));
+  assert.ok(torsionResponse("end", r, 0.03).twist > 10 * torsionResponse("centre", r, 0.03).twist);
+  assert.ok(torsionResponse("end", r, 0.15).twist < torsionResponse("end", r, 0.03).twist / 3);
+  // Below and above the resonance the twist is far smaller.
+  assert.ok(torsionResponse("end", r * 0.6, 0.03).twist < torsionResponse("end", r, 0.03).twist / 3);
+  assert.ok(torsionResponse("end", r * 1.3, 0.03).twist < torsionResponse("end", r, 0.03).twist / 3);

Scripted Wikimedia image downloads (generic UA) got HTTP 429; the Commons API itself works. On 2026-11-18 the user approved fetching the stop photos through their Chrome (Claude in Chrome: navigate to the upload.wikimedia.org file, fetch → blob → `<a download>`), and they clicked Chrome's "allow multiple downloads" prompt themselves.

**Why:** spoofing a browser UA in a script was refused as unauthorized; the user's real browser at human pace is fine.
On 2026-11-19 Chrome silently blocked every download after the first in a batch; what worked was fetching all files on an upload.wikimedia.org page (API via `origin=*`), packing them into one tar in JS, and downloading that single file.

**How to apply:** still ask before each new download batch (names, source, size). Use upload.wikimedia.org paths (thumbs live under /thumb/ there too). Move the files out of ~/Downloads into the scratchpad afterwards. In Chrome, call the Commons API with fetch from a commons.wikimedia.org page (works where scripts are throttled); the extension blocks results containing URLs with query strings, so return titles/paths only.

I handled the new proposals from `docs/bilingual-copy-and-ux-proposals.md`, except the W 196 R 3-D wind tunnel. The dev server is running on :8765 and your Chrome has the W 196 R stop open; I haven't looked at the new panels in a browser yet. Unit tests (233) and e2e tests (277) pass, and screenshots of each changed view show 56–60 fps and no page errors. Nothing is committed or pushed.

**Daimler van radiator**
- The step now asks which system cools the water down as you drive. Both start from 90 °C water, 16 km/h and 60 % load.
- The tubular radiator and the plain tank now run at the same time. A shared trace shows both water temperatures, and the radiator's water settles at 80 °C while the tank's climbs to boiling. A "Start again at 90 °C" button resets both.
- On the tubular radiator, air passes through the tubes and the water flows between them. With the tank, the air splits and flows around it.
- The legend now marks the metal wall the heat passes through.
- The stop got a question for the route card, an opening "look" line and a closing line.

**Engines** (the maths is new and tested)
- **300 SL:** a new "Engine balance" step. Arrows show each piston's push on the block and their total. You can switch between once and twice per turn, and step 30° at a time. Readouts compare the six with an inline four, whose twice-per-turn pushes add up.
- **770:** the engine step now asks whether you can still pick out single power strokes. It has a torque trace at the crank: the eight against an even-firing six, at the same mean torque, firing 200 and 150 times a second at 3,000 rpm.
- **W 196 R:** a new engine step for the M 196. You can choose drive from the middle or drive from the end, sweep the engine speed and set the damping. A chart plots crank twist against rpm, and purple witness marks on the crank show the twist 100× enlarged.
  - The end drive resonates near 6,800 rpm in this model; the middle drive has no resonance in the 2,000–9,000 rpm range.
  - Illustrative and listed on the stop as unverified: the stiffness and other twist-model values, the firing order, the conrod length and the 53° tilt.

**Real-part photos (7):** each is cropped and stored in `parts/`, with captions in both languages. The licences match the doc.

| Stop | Photo |
|---|---|
| Daimler van | Maybach's 1897 radiator drawing |
| 300 SLR | Ducati desmo rockers |
| 600 | Citroën accumulator in section |
| 260 D | Ganz–Jendrassik head in section |
| 300 SL (balance step) | Six-cylinder block and crankshaft |
| Velo | Belt-shifting handles |
| SLK | Roof halfway through folding |

I worded the Ganz caption cautiously: it says only that the engine has a small chamber joined to the cylinder by a narrow outlet. I couldn't confirm it burns fuel there first.
